_comment: THE COVERAGE LOCATIONS — ONE LIST, EVERY SURFACE THAT SHOWS THEM.
Client 2026-08-14 (Einsatzgebiete 1): 'build it so the map/pill list updates
automatically when we add new coverage locations (single data source)'.
Before this file the same list was maintained by hand in FOUR places and they
had already drifted: partials/coverage-chips.html, the second chip row inside
pages/index.html, partials/footer-de.html, the CITIES table in
docs/design-sources/franken-map.py and the coverageLocations object in
js/coverage-map.js. Adding a city meant five edits and remembering all five.
WHO READS THIS FILE:
build.js .................. renders the pill lists into real static HTML at
build time (<!-- coverage: … --> markers), and
copies this list to dist/assets/data/
coverage-locations.json for the runtime map.
js/coverage-map.js ........ fetches that published copy and builds the
Leaflet markers/boundaries from it.
docs/design-sources/
franken-map.py ............ reads it to regenerate /einsatzgebiete/'s inline
hero SVG (dev-time; paste the output).
TO ADD A LOCATION: add an entry here, drop its boundary geojson in
assets/data/coverage-boundaries/, run `npm run build`. The pills and both
Leaflet maps follow automatically. The /einsatzgebiete/ hero SVG is the one
surface that is NOT automatic — it is inline vector art, so re-run
franken-map.py and paste. That is deliberate: it is generated once in
development, never at runtime (CLAUDE.md).
FIELDS:
href .... null means NO CITY PAGE. Those render as <button> pills that only
drive the map, never as links — 'render without links' is the
client's own instruction and 'do not ship a linked 404' is the
standing rule. Give it a URL the day the page exists and it
promotes itself everywhere.
row ..... which of the two chip rows it belongs to (the footer-matching
split). Ignored for entries without an href.
center .. [latitude, longitude], Leaflet's order. The .geojson files keep
GeoJSON's own [lon, lat] — nothing reverses that.
map ..... the /einsatzgebiete/ hero SVG only. `side` is which way the label
runs from the pin ('start' = to the right, 'end' = to the left) and
exists to keep neighbouring labels from colliding; `major` is pin
SIZE, for the four regional centres.
